items.title: Sumner Labat Interview, 1962-11-11
items.q: Interviewer mentions 'Fusche' and 'Al Fusche' in the context of Sam Horgan and Skeeter, but the interviewee (Sumner Labat) does not claim a personal relationship, collaboration, or direct interaction with Al Fusche in the provided text.

ctx.x: Yes, ma'am, it does. I made money with me, too. That's right.

How many different kinds of clarinets have you owned? Have you owned a C and a B flat and an E flat and all the different kinds, or you always played with one kind? One kind. Which kind is that, a B flat? B flat, E flat. Oh, they're a B flat clarinet like you see today, most of the time. Al but a band? Al but a band. Al but a band. Al but a band. How many keys? Do you remember? I used 13. 13. It's a real old, old one. I used to hold Al without the ring. Yeah. You still have it?

No, I gave it away. I have a brother. I have a brother who teaches at Isaiah University. Oh, yeah? He's been there about, oh, 30 years, almost. He's been a professor here about 30 years. His son was taking up saxophone, you see. And after I gave it up, I brought the clarinet over to him and gave it to him. He said maybe he could make some use of it to see because I wasn't going to play anymore. What was he playing?

items.title: Sumner Labat Interview, 1962-11-11
items.q: The interviewee (Sumner Labat) does not mention Red boy Alton. The interviewer mentions 'Red boy Alton' in the context of identifying 'Skeeter' (Al Fusche), stating 'That's right. Red boy Alton. Alton. From Mobile, Alabama.' The interviewee confirms the name 'Alton' but does not provide any personal

ctx.x: You know one used to use horn mute? Sam Horgan. I never seen a man use mutes like Sam Horgan. He knew what to do with them though. Sam had a good plan.

Yeah, well I know he was good, even with what everybody says. You can tell it on the record but he must have been better, because he made that record in 1927 I think. And I think he'd already had one stroke at least or something. It's hard to tell what he was like. You know? Good. After he had that boy stroke he was dragging. Yeah, he was dragging. That's when he had Skeeter with him. Who's Skeeter? Well, Fusche. That's right. Red boy Alton. Alton. From Mobile, Alabama. I never will forget that. Because he's on…
Third and that man lying there.
